title: epan: Fix out-of-bounds reads in 22 dissectors due to missing tvb length checks
description:
Add bounds checks to while-loops that scan tvb data for sentinel values without verifying remaining captured length. These could read past the end of the packet buffer with malformed or truncated packets, causing crashes.

The recurring pattern fixed:

```
while (tvb_get_uint8(tvb, offset) != SENTINEL) // unsafe 
while (tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset) > 0 && tvb_get_uint8(tvb, offset) != SENTINEL) // safe
```

Also corrected several instances of the wrong idiom: 

```
offset < tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset) // WRONG
tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset) > 0 // correct 
```

(tvb_captured_length_remaining returns bytes remaining, not total length)

AI-Assisted: yes (Kiro)

notes.body:
> `while (tvb_captured_length_remaining(tvb, offset) > 0 && tvb_get_uint8(tvb, offset) != SENTINEL) // safe`

"Safe" as in "won't run past the end of a tvbuff", but that also means it won't report that it stopped dissecting because the packet capture was cut short by slicing.

And `tvb_get_uint8()` should throw an exception if `offset` is past the end of the captured data in `tvb`; that exception will cause the dissection process to report that it stopped dissecting because the packet capture was cut short by slicing.

The only problems I see are:

1. if the offset is signed rather than unsigned, you run the risk of signed overflow;
2. if the offset is unsigned, you run the risk of wrapping around.

1) should ideally be fixed by using unsigned offsets; @johnthacker has been doing some work to have more routines take unsigned offsets (the ultimate goal is to have them *all* take unsigned offsets, but there might be some residual use of negative offsets to mean offsets from the end of the buffer, so that takes some care).

2) should perhaps be handled by (inline) routines that do a checked add to an offset and, if the check fails, throw a `ReportedBoundsError` exception.
okej, then most of these are actually not relevant? Or what do you say

> okej, then most of these are actually not relevant?

Preventing the `offset` argument to a tvb routine is not necessary to prevent accessing beyond the end of the buffer for the tvbuff, and hence not necessary to prevent accesses past the end of the packet buffer, unless there is an error in the low-level tvbuff code.

If there's an error in the low-level tvbuff code, that would need to be fixed there. However, that code is fairly straightforward.
